problems: The road, pedestrian paving, lot borders and ivory objects are all close in value. Road and square merge, so the circulation hierarchy is lost at stream scale.
elements.fix: Keep the ivory palette but set value bands: vehicle lane a mid cool grey (#b9c4cc), pedestrian paving the lightest ivory, lot borders a soft sage, and continuous darker guide seams (#5f7d86) at least 0.15 m wide at the road edges. These must read without bloom.

problems: The floating amber loop is pale and thin against the pale sage lot and nearly disappears in the vignette.
elements.fix: Make the loop thicker (around 0.15 m section) and a more saturated amber (#e89a1c, glow). Put it on a dark navy emitter pedestal with a dark shadow disc beneath, and raise it to about 1.2 m so it silhouettes against the ground.

problems: The 'solid-light' crossing reads as an opaque white panel bridge with railings, more a recolour of the Modern bridge than projected technology.
elements.fix: Add substantial dark emitter blocks at both bank anchors and a translucent-looking cyan glow deck, made of thin glow slabs with gaps, not opaque white panels. Use luminous edge rails instead of white posts. Keep the deck alignment and length.

problems: The 'Crescent Dock Hover Seat' is a small purple arc on a puck. At stream scale it reads as a toy or a banana, not a bench at human scale.
elements.fix: Make it a full 1.8-2 m curved ivory bench with a visible seat and backrest, hovering 0.15 m over a dark navy dock base with a glow ring. Keep the purple only as a cushion accent.

problems: The six home examples (and café and tower) are framed on independent plinths, so there is no shared 16 m lot footprint or door/access anchor proving they occupy the same plot.
elements.fix: Render each age's home, café and tower on the same 16 m lot template. Mark the lot outline and the door/path anchor at the same position, with the street on the same side, in every age.
